text: Dead Branch makes exhaust the engine: after getting it, favour cards that exhaust or play many 0-cost skills (Corruption, Dark Embrace, Feel No Pain, True Grit+, Sever Soul, Offering, Sentinel). Corruption + Dead Branch + Dark Embrace carried an A5 win.

When most cards put new cards into the hand (Dead Branch, Dark Embrace, Offering), the default draw stop interrupts almost every action. Use stop_on="choice,spawn" for sequences made only of cards already in hand, put card-adding cards last, and plan the new cards on the next call. Keep draw on when the rest of the turn depends on what arrives (short on energy, Fiend Fire / Sever Soul, hand near 10).

Buffer (Fossilized Helix) is used up by self-inflicted HP loss too (Offering, Bloodletting). If the first enemy hit is big, play those after it, or accept losing the Buffer only when the energy/draw is worth more than the hit.

Time Eater: Time Warp counts cards across turns and ends your turn at 12, so check the counter at turn start and spend the few cards left on the biggest hits. Below half HP it heals back to half on its next turn (BUFF intent), so damage past that line that turn is wasted; save the burst for after. Orange Pellets (power+attack+skill in one turn) clears its debuffs on you.

Hand letters are not in order once new cards arrive (e.g. f c e u v). Re-read the letter next to the card name before sending; I played Second Wind thinking it was Offering and exhausted my own Offering and Double Tap.

Darklings: a dead one shows as (reviving) and comes back at half HP on the enemy turn unless all are dead. Lower them evenly with AoE, then finish all in the same turn; finishing the last one before their turn wins even if the others are still 'reviving'.

Don't take an Act 1 elite below ~50% HP with a starter-ish deck. I entered Lagavulin (110 HP) at 24/80 to reach a rest right after and died on F8, 1 damage short. Lagavulin hits 18-20 twice per 3 turns; a deck dealing ~20/turn needs ~5 turns, so it costs ~40+ HP. Pick the path whose elite comes after a rest, or a ? room, when HP is low. Hitting a sleeping Lagavulin wakes it; it skips that enemy turn, then attacks 18+ the next. Once awake it has no Metallicize block.

On the map, choose <n> takes the index in the "Next:" list, not the map column. "Next: 0 M(x1) 1 M(x3) 2 M(x4) 3 M(x6)" -> choose 1 goes to column 3. I typed choose 3 meaning column 3, landed on column 6 and lost the planned early shop route (ran into two elites instead).

When planning a route, check each planned room's onward exits, not just the room. In Act 2 I planned "? then elite if HP>60%", but that ? (col5>6) led ONLY to the elite, so I entered Gremlin Leader at 24/79 with no choice (won, barely). If a room has a single exit to an elite, decide at the previous fork with current HP.

Collector (A5, 282 HP) killed me on F33 from 48/79. Pattern seen: T1 summon 2 Torchheads (~39 HP, hit 7 then 10 each), Collector hits 21, then on ~T4 a STRONG DEBUFF (3 Vulnerable/Weak/Frail on me), then it resummons and hits 31 + 2x10 = ~51 with Vulnerable. Plan the whole fight around that debuff turn: kill Torchheads with AoE (Immolate/Combust/Cleave) by T3, keep the big block (Ghostly Armor, Power Through, potions like Dexterity) for the turn AFTER the debuff, and enter with 60+ HP. A deck with ~30 damage/turn and no Disarm/Shockwave/Flame Barrier cannot outlast it.

Berserk's Vulnerable is expensive at A5: playing it on turn 1 in front of 2+ attackers cost me 7-11 extra HP several times in Act 2 (Centurion+Mystic took me 42->20). Play Berserk on a turn when enemies are not attacking (buff/debuff intents), or skip it in short fights.

Writhing Mass (Act 3, 160 HP, Reactive + Malleable): every hit that gets through its block re-rolls its intent, and it won't repeat a move. Its big hit is ~38 (more with my Vulnerable). When the shown intent is survivable and blocking can cover it, don't attack after blocking, since a re-roll can land on the big hit. Front-load damage on its non-attack turns (Implant/debuff). I went 51 -> 11 HP against it.

Necronomicon (Cursed Tome event, ~16 HP total) was worth it: the first 2+ cost attack each turn is played twice. Immolate+ x2 (56-60 AoE) cleared whole Act 2/3 hallway fights in one card, Perfected Strike/Heavy Blade+ x2 did 48-84, and Whirlwind with X>=2 counts too. A card made 0-cost this turn (Attack Potion) is NOT doubled. Gremlin Horn after multi-kills gives the energy back.

Collector (A5): T1 spawns 2 Torch Heads (8 each/turn), T2 fireball ~22, T4 Mega Debuff (Weak+Vuln+Frail 3), T5+ fireball ~25-31 with your Vulnerable. Save Impervious/big block for the turns AFTER the debuff, kill one Torch Head early to cut 8/turn, and Disarm the Collector. Combust's 1 HP/turn self-damage becomes lethal once HP is in single digits - don't play it in a boss fight at low Max HP.

Act 2 A5 hallway fights cost me 15-35 HP each with a block-light deck (Mugger+Looter, Chosen, 3 Cultists, Byrd+Chosen, Shelled Parasite+Fungi). Prioritise block cards (Shrug, Flame Barrier, Impervious) and a removal over more attacks in late Act 1/early Act 2, and use a Lee's Waffle / shop heal when HP < 35%.
